lines: // claudeVersionTimeout bounds one `claude --version` run: the first run of a newly written
// binary costs ~11 s on macOS (kb:fact/new-claude-binary-first-run-slow-on-macos).
keeps.reason: Without it a reader would shorten the 30 s timeout to a few seconds as generous for `claude --version`; that makes the ~11 s first run of a new binary time out and report unknown at `const claudeVersionTimeout = 30 * time.Second`.

lines: // seen and haveSeen belong to the loop goroutine alone.
keeps.reason: Without it a reader would read seen/haveSeen from another goroutine such as Current without a lock; that races with the unlocked writes at `f.seen, f.haveSeen = id, true`.

anchor.text: func prepareServing(ctx context.Context, f *cliFlags, st *store.Store, log zerolog.Logger) (*servingEnv, error) {

lines: // prepareServing bootstraps the tokens, binds the listener and writes the tokens file and
// hook wrapper scripts — in that order, since each step's output feeds the next.
// ClaudeVersionConfig groups the Claude Code version watch's config. Poll <= 0 means no
// check ever runs, so `claude` is never exec'd by a zero-value Config.
// Poll is how often the resolved claude binary's identity is looked at (a stat, never a
// claude run). <= 0 disables the watch: hello.claudeCode stays "unknown".
// ClaudeCodeInfo is the daemon's latest Claude Code version check against the
// canary-verified range (kb:anchor/ws.hello, kb:anchor/ws.claude-code), also read by the
// issue-capture snapshot. Installed is nil iff Status is "unknown" (not checked yet, or the
// check failed, hung past its timeout or was unparseable); Floor/Verified are always
// populated.
// claudeCodeMessage is the WS `claudeCode` envelope (kb:anchor/ws.claude-code): the same
// object as hello.claudeCode, sent only when the daemon's result changed — never per look,
// never with a timestamp.
// claudeVersionFeature owns the daemon's latest Claude Code version result
// (kb:adr/connection-claude-version-watched-and-pushed). It mounts no routes. Its one
// goroutine (bgLoop) is the only writer of current, under mu; hello and the issue snapshot
// read it through Current. No outcome here makes musterd skip serving
// (kb:adr/connection-installed-claude-classified-never-refused).
// Current returns the latest result; "unknown" with Installed nil until the first check
// finishes.
/** WS `claudeCode`: the daemon's check result changed after this hello — re-renders the
* version readout alone. */
// kb:anchor/ws.claude-code: sent only when the daemon's latest check result changed — the
// same object `hello.claudeCode` carries, nested under `claudeCode`.
// tick looks at the binary's identity and runs one check when it is not the one last
// checked. An identity that cannot be resolved (no claude on PATH, a bad -claude-bin, an
// update mid-swap) runs nothing and keeps the held value; it is logged once per
// unresolved stretch and the next tick looks again. The identity is recorded before the
// check so a binary that changes while it runs is seen again by the next tick.
keeps.reason: Without it a reader would move `f.seen, f.haveSeen = id, true` below the check call as tidier ordering; that makes a binary swapped during the check go unnoticed at `report := f.check(checkCtx)`.

lines: /** The text/warning decision per `ClaudeCodeInfo.status`:
* - `null` (pre-hello) -> "claude unknown", no warning, the unknown hover text
* - `status: "unknown"` (any `installed`), or a defensive non-`unknown` status with
*   `installed === null` (the daemon never sends this — kb:adr/connection-installed-claude-classified-never-refused) -> "claude
*   unknown", no warning, the unknown hover text
* - `status: "verified"` -> "claude <installed>", no warning
* - `status: "above"` -> "claude <installed>" + the "not tested" warning
* - `status: "below"` -> "claude <installed>" + the "not tested, please update" warning
keeps.reason: Edited on `main`; still true: `export function describeClaudeVersion(info: ClaudeCodeInfo | null)` returns the unknown, above, below and verified results the comment lists.
